assertions.name: the_scored_value_is_a_DIFFERENCE_of_two_word_traces
assertions.source: reconstructing nuc11_interleaved letter by letter gives tr(p) = 0.629328402202921918 and tr(n) = 0.475133517155682213; NEITHER matches the census witness's tr_conv_D = -0.1541948850472397056592555, and their DIFFERENCE matches it to 1.41e-26. delta_of's docstring says so independently: 'Delta = neutron - proton, coordinatewise in the NF basis'

assertions.name: a_lower_bound_on_each_word_does_NOT_bound_their_difference
assertions.source: tr is linear, so tr(Delta) = tr(n) - tr(p). Two quantities each >= 1 have a difference bounded by nothing. The inference drawn on this branch -- that tr_M >= 1 per PSD-feasible gamma-gamma word excludes Q_beta at every strand count -- does not follow and is WITHDRAWN. Asserted as a check so the retraction is machine-recorded rather than living only in prose

assertions.name: the_difference_predictions_STRADDLE_the_target
assertions.source: all 15 pairs of the six-element feasible set run from -100.0 % to 79.39829 % -- they straddle the measurement rather than sitting above it, which is the opposite of what the retracted claim said. Reported in full; reporting only the closest would be selection against the target

assertions.name: the_best_difference_is_the_same_ORDER_as_chance
assertions.source: 11 distinct |differences| over the 15 pairs, 4 within +-50 % of the target, median spacing 0.0571821 -> expected best-by-chance 7.725 %. Observed best 5.14884 %. Better than chance but the same order, on a grid of 11 values -- not evidence for any pair, and the assertion deliberately tests ORDER rather than 'beats chance', because beating a coarse grid is what a coarse grid does

assertions.name: the_per_word_bound_itself_is_untouched
assertions.source: tr_M >= 1 still holds on every PSD-feasible gamma-gamma word (1.0, 1.032897756, 1.137405209, 1.073238808, 1.073238808, 1.331992493), tight at the empty word. The det-1 fact, AM-GM, weight non-negativity and the Markov normalisation are all measured and all stand; so do the floor and every Lean theorem on this branch, which are about pairings and PSD matrices and mention no observable. What is withdrawn is one inference, not the mathematics

assertions.name: the_scored_elements_words_are_BOTH_psd_infeasible
assertions.source: nuc11_interleaved fails Matrix.PosSemidef on ['(2, 1)', '(1, 1, 1)'] for the proton and ['(2, 1)', '(1, 1, 1)'] for the neutron -- 2 of 3 H_3 blocks each -- and carries det != 1 in every block (proton: {'(3,)': '1.38249446339', '(2, 1)': '-1.02197249381', '(1, 1, 1)': '-0.739223570776'}). 🛑 That is a MEASUREMENT under reading (B), NOT a rejection by the ruling: the SDP scope question was answered '(A) core only' (bean qou-99qc, 2026-09-12), under which reading 3 prunes nothing outside the gamma-gamma core and 'the census element stands'. The first draft of this assertion said the ruling excluded it; that was an over-application of the SDP half. The alternating-character exclusion already recorded is separate and unaffected

description: RETRACTION. Q_beta = |eps(Delta)|*E_0 with Delta = NEUTRON word MINUS PROTON word (delta_of's own docstring, confirmed to 25 digits here), and the Markov trace is linear -- so the tr_M >= 1 bound on individual PSD-feasible gamma-gamma words does NOT bound the scored quantity, and the 'cannot reproduce Q_beta at any strand count' inference drawn from it on this branch is withdrawn. The bound itself, the floor, and every Lean theorem stand: they are about pairings and PSD matrices and none mentions Q_beta. Caught by the calibration step. What the difference functional actually gives, all 15 pairs reported: -100 % to +79.4 %, STRADDLING the target rather than sitting above it, best +5.15 % against 7.73 % expected by chance. Surviving new MEASUREMENT: the scored element's proton and neutron words are both PSD-INFEASIBLE (2 of 3 blocks) with det != 1 everywhere -- which is reading (B), NOT a rejection by the ruling, whose scope answer was '(A) core only'.
